criteria.name: Communication

descriptors.0: Nothing reached the channel while the incident was open, or only after the lead had to chase you repeatedly.
descriptors.1: You posted, but late or without saying what was wrong; the lead had to ask and nudge.
descriptors.2: Some timely updates, but at least one gap or one post that did not say what you had found.
descriptors.3: Prompt, useful updates with one slip: a late answer to the lead, or a quiet stretch.
descriptors.4: A first update in the first two minutes, the lead's request answered at once, no quiet stretch, and the cause named in plain words.

criteria.keep: Keep posting a short status as soon as you know something, even when it is only 'still looking'.

rules.advice: Post a first update in the channel within two minutes, even if it is only what you have seen so far.
When the lead asks for an update, answer within a minute, even if nothing has changed.
Set a timer for each promised update: do not let five quiet minutes pass without a post.
Say what you found, not only that you are working on it: name the column, the migration or the file.

criteria.name: Diagnosis

descriptors.0: You changed code before you had run the tests or opened anything that explains the failure.
descriptors.1: You found the failing call but never looked at what changed in the database.
descriptors.2: You looked at the right places, but after you had already started editing, or only with a pointer.
descriptors.3: Reproduce, read the route, read the migration: three of the four habits, in order.
descriptors.4: You reproduced the failure, read the failing route and the migration before the first edit, and needed no pointer.

criteria.keep: Keep reproducing first and reading what changed before you touch a file.

rules.advice: Run the tests and read the first error line of each failure before you change anything.
Open the file named in the error and find the failing call before you edit.
Something changed on Monday: read the newest migration in database/migrations before you edit.
Look at what changed in the database yourself before you wait for a teammate to point at it.

criteria.name: Fix quality

descriptors.0: The fix is missing, or the suite is still red on main.
descriptors.1: Part of the problem is fixed, but the old column name is still used or the change is much larger than the problem.
descriptors.2: The suite is green, but the change was sent back, or it left the old name behind.
descriptors.3: A correct, small fix accepted with one thing to improve.
descriptors.4: Every use of the old column name changed, the whole suite green on my re-run, a small change, and no send-back.

criteria.keep: Keep changing only what the problem needs, and searching for every use of a renamed name.

rules.advice: Search the whole backend folder for the old name before you submit: the same name can be used in more than one file.
Run the whole suite, not only the acceptance tests, before you submit.
Change only the lines the rename needs; a small change is easier to review and safer to ship.
Read your own diff the way the Reviewer will before you submit, so it does not come back with items.

criteria.name: Testing

descriptors.0: You submitted without ever running the tests, and nothing protects the fix.
descriptors.1: You ran the tests, but not green before submitting, and nothing protects the fix.
descriptors.2: A green run before submit and no red submit, but no new test that proves the fix.
descriptors.3: Green before submit, no red submit, and a regression test that was added but does not prove the fix.
descriptors.4: A green run before submit, no red submit, and a regression test that fails on the broken code and passes on yours.

criteria.keep: Keep adding a regression test with every bug fix: it is the part that outlives the incident.

rules.advice: Run the tests yourself and see them green before you press Submit.
Submit only when your own run is green: a red submit costs a round trip.
Add a regression test in tests/regression/ for the bug you fixed.
Run your new test before you fix the code: it has to be red then, and green after the fix.

criteria.name: Ownership

descriptors.0: The fix was not accepted, or it came long after the clinic opened with no word to the team.
descriptors.1: Accepted late, with many hints and no word to the team.
descriptors.2: Accepted, but you leaned on hints or went outside your files.
descriptors.3: Accepted in time, you stayed inside your files and asked for little help, but you did not close the loop.
descriptors.4: Accepted inside the time box, inside your own files, with one hint at most, and the team told that the fix was ready.

criteria.keep: Keep telling the team when the fix is ready and what you did.

rules.advice: Watch the clock: the clinic opens at 09:00, so aim to have the fix submitted inside the time box.
Try the next step on your own before you ask a teammate; every answer counts as a hint.
Read the list of files you may edit in the task document before you change anything outside it.
When the tests are green, tell the channel the fix is ready and what you changed.
